text:
opsbot: ALERT: service=redwood-gateway-usw2 severity=sev2 elevated 5xx rate and request timeouts detected for /v1/generate and /v1/chat. Rolling 5m 5xx rate = 7.8% (baseline 0.3%).
alertbot: Page sent to @maya oncall (pagerduty). incident id: INC-1998765432. runbook: https://internal/runbooks/scheduler-hol
maya: I’m on it. starting triage. first look at scheduler queue depths and batching metrics.
maya: Grafana: scheduler_queue_depth spikes to 12k across pool-scheduler-*-usw2. p95 latency jumping 1.2s -> 4.8s. many reqs timing out at gateway.
sam: seeing similar from logs. gateway shows 502/504s when backend timeout triggers. sample logs:
```
2026-02-12T02:14:21Z Gateway: upstream timeout to scheduler-1 addr=10.2.14.22 req_id=abc123
Batcher: blocking on head_of_line backlog=12467 waiting_for_capacity
```
lee: initial hypothesis: batching scheduler overloaded -> head-of-line blocking causing backlog and upstream timeouts. maybe runaway large batches + reduced flush rate.
tess: any deploys/rollouts in the last 30m? eng-runtime-oncall: nope, no recent rollout. autoscaler didn't add nodes -- looks like scale is inhibited by a quota spike.
maya: ok mitigation plan: 1) reduce max_batch_size at gateway to force smaller batches 2) enable fallback routing to backup-dedicated pool 3) temporarily increase scheduler concurrency and drop long-waiting requests (head-of-line eviction) 4) notify customers. executing in that order.
jordan: I can flip routing to backup pool if needed. @maya please coordinate.
maya: kicking off step 1. patching gateway config:
```
PATCH /configs/gateway/global
{"max_batch_size": 8, "max_wait_ms": 30}
```
maya: applying now.
opsbot: deploy started: config-update gateway/global by maya.
lee: pushed config looks applied to 7/9 gateways, some still at old config due to control-plane propagation.
sam: starting step 2: enabling backup-route for traffic overflow to dedicated-pool-usw2-b. routing policy set to overflow when queue_depth > 1000.
eng-runtime-oncall: note - backup pool has lower throughput for some models, may increase token cost and slight latency.
tess: can we also throttle incoming high-rate clients? customer-success: we already received first support ticket referencing 504s from app X. tagging customers on the affected endpoints.
maya: temporarily enabling global rate limiter for anonymous keys to 60 rps per token.
opsbot: rate-limiter rule applied.
jordan: backup route enabled. traffic started spilling. observing p95 drop from 4.8s -> 2.1s, 5xx rate down to 3.2%.
lee: running targeted restarts for scheduler-worker pods exhibiting OOMs/blocked threads. kubectl commands: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/scheduler-worker -n redwood-inference`
sam: restarts in progress; some workers came up healthy but a few got stuck on warmup due to KV cache warm path. infra-bot: auto-scaler noticed warmup lag, spin-up limited by instance quota.
maya: summary of immediate mitigations completed: reduced batch size, enabled backup routing, rate limits applied, restarts kicked. still seeing elevated errors but trending down.
jordan: starting customer impact assessment. affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. estimated affected requests in 5m window ~ 18k, errors ~ 1.4k. high-impact customers: partner-app-x (partial errors) and enterprise-cust-y (timeouts).
customer-success: notified partner-app-x and enterprise-cust-y. CS case numbers created.
tess: runbook step: perform head-of-line eviction to drop requests waiting > 25s. executing now on queue-manager.
opsbot: command executed: queue-manager evict --threshold=25s --policy=oldest-first; evicted 3,200 stale requests.
lee: after eviction, immediate backlog dropped to ~2.1k. 5xx fell to 1.1% and p95 latency ~1.6s.
eng-runtime-oncall: recommendation to roll back any large-batch config changes we made last week and disable eager aggregation. suggest follow-up config task.
maya: agree. scheduling a post-incident change to tune aggregation heuristics and add queue_depth-based autoscaling triggers.
jordan: escalation: opening incident bridge with eng-runtime and infra. join link: https://meet.internal/bridge/INC-1998765432
sam: logs show a repeating stack trace in scheduler: `AcquireBatchTimeoutException` from BatchScheduler.handle() when backlog > 10k. adding to incident timeline.
tess: will create an alert rule to fire earlier: alert when queue_depth > 500 for > 2m.
opsbot: timeline updated. incident severity remains SEV2. paging to on-call SRE and platform leads.
jordan: Handing over to @jordan for next shift in 20m. @maya stand by for postmortem notes.
maya: handing off. current status: mitigations holding, 5xx ~0.9%, still monitoring for regressions. follow-ups: change autoscale policy, tune max_batch_size heuristics, add head-of-line early eviction, capacity quota check with infra.
jordan: I’m on takeover. thanks @maya. I’ll keep the bridge open and update every 15m until steady. final note for ticket: incident_root_cause = temporary scheduler saturation due to sudden high incoming burst combined with aggregation config + quota-limited autoscaling -> head-of-line blocking -> gateway timeouts.
customer-success: update sent to customers at 02:48 UTC: short-lived errors, mitigations applied, follow-up postmortem will be shared.
opsbot: INCIDENT CLOSED (transferred to monitoring) at 1998767020. Please file postmortem: /pm/INC-1998765432
